1. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned A.P.P. for the State.
2. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that an application of jointness has been filed as the notice on behalf of the O.P. No.2 was received by her father-in-law.

It is next submitted that the father of the petitioner did not receive the notice on behalf of the O.P. No.2 rather the new father-in-law of the O.P. No.2 received the notice on her behalf, as such, an application of jointness has been filed.

The learned counsel for the petitioner thus submits that when O.P. No.2 has performed her second marriage, no useful purpose would be served by keeping the present anticipatory bail application pending.

Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.621 of 2023(9)
dt.13-03-2024 3.

The learned APP at this stage submits that the petitioner seeks anticipatory bail in a case registered under sections 498A, 323, 342, 313 and 34 of the I.P.C. read with Sections 3 & 4 of the D.P. Act and the punishment for the aforesaid offences is less than 7 years.
This submission of the learned APP is not disputed by the learned counsel for the petitioner.

The learned APP further submits that if what has been submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner about the second Rajesh Yadav vs The State Of Bihar on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154866518/
1 marriage of O.P. No.2 the same can be brought to the notice of the I.O. as it has been submitted by learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner that the investigation of the case is still going on.
